name: The Mohorovičić Discontinuity
statement: The Moho is the seismic-velocity boundary separating Earth's crust from the underlying mantle, averaging about 35 km deep beneath continents.
statementAccent: Earth's crust from the underlying mantle
meaning: The Moho marks the depth where seismic wave speeds abruptly increase as waves pass from lower-density crustal rock into denser mantle rock. It is not a single fixed depth worldwide but varies with crust type, lying much shallower beneath oceans than beneath continents.
mechanism: Andrija Mohorovičić identified the boundary when seismograms from a 1909 earthquake near Zagreb showed two sets of P- and S-wave arrivals at distant stations: one travelling directly through the crust, and a second, faster set that had refracted off a deeper, denser layer before returning. This velocity discontinuity, caused by the change from crustal basalt/granite to mantle peridotite, defines the Moho.

examples.text: Mohorovičić discovered the discontinuity by analysing records from the 8 October 1909 earthquake near Pokupsko, Croatia, comparing wave arrival times across central Europe.
The Moho lies roughly 5–10 km below the seafloor under ocean basins but 20–90 km deep beneath continents (averaging about 35 km), reflecting the much thinner oceanic crust.
The Soviet Kola Superdeep Borehole (1970–1992) reached 12,262 metres, far short of the Moho there, before high rock temperatures around 180°C forced the project to stop.

whyItMatters: The Moho gives geologists a clear, seismically detectable definition of where crust ends and mantle begins, underpinning models of plate tectonics, crustal thickness, and the structure of continents versus ocean basins. It also motivated ambitious drilling efforts, such as Project Mohole, aimed at sampling mantle rock.
limits: The Moho is defined seismically, by a velocity jump, rather than strictly by composition, and in some settings the transition is gradational rather than sharp, making its exact depth harder to pin down. No borehole has yet physically reached it.
misreadings: It is sometimes described as the boundary of "crust ending and molten rock beginning," but the underlying mantle at that depth is solid peridotite, not magma. It is also sometimes assumed to be a uniform global depth, when it varies severalfold between oceanic and continental settings.
origin: Discovered by Croatian seismologist Andrija Mohorovičić in 1909, from his analysis of the 8 October 1909 earthquake near Zagreb.

sources.text: Mohorovičić discontinuity, Wikipedia. — the 1909 discovery, the refracted/direct wave method, and continental versus oceanic depths.
Kola Superdeep Borehole, Wikipedia. — the 12,262 m depth reached and that the Moho was not reached due to high temperatures.
